seo.title: Four Seasons I: Suites, Sailings and Fares on Four Seasons Yachts' First Yacht | James Wild & Co
seo.description: Four Seasons I carries up to 222 guests in 95 suites, a 207-metre yacht sailing the Mediterranean in summer and the Caribbean and Bahamas in winter. All 14 suite types, 115 published sailings to October 2028, each day by day, and fares from US$12,200 per suite.

tagline: Ninety-five suites, each with its own terrace, and a marina that opens onto the sea.
answer: Four Seasons I is the first yacht from Four Seasons Yachts, in service since 20 March 2026. She is 207 metres (679 feet) long, with 95 suites on 15 decks for up to 222 guests and a guest-to-staff ratio of one to one. She sails the Mediterranean in summer and the Caribbean and the Bahamas in winter, on voyages of 3 to 18 nights. Fares are published per suite for the whole voyage, in US dollars, from US$12,200.

Mediterranean in summer; Caribbean and Bahamas in winter
Per suite, for the voyage, in USD
overview: Four Seasons I entered service on 20 March 2026, the first of the yachts Four Seasons is building. She is 207 metres long and 34,000 gross tons, and carries no more than 222 guests in 95 suites, with one member of staff for every guest.

Every suite has a terrace. They run from the 44 square metre Seaview Suite to the Funnel Suite, 501 square metres on four levels, with its own splash pool, gym and kitchen. More than 100 combinations of suites connect, so a family or a party of friends can take a run of rooms together; the Loft Suite joins with up to seven others for as many as 20 guests.

On deck there is an outdoor pool, and at the waterline a transverse marina that opens on both sides of the yacht for swimming and watersports. She spends the summer in the Mediterranean, from the Greek islands and the Adriatic to the Rivieras, crosses the Atlantic in spring and autumn, and winters in the Lesser Antilles and the Bahamas.

Four Seasons Yachts prices each voyage by the suite, not by the person. The fare covers the suite, breakfast, Wi-Fi, the marina's watersports and taxes and port fees; lunch, dinner and alcoholic drinks are charged as taken.

faqs: How many guests does Four Seasons I carry?
Up to 222, in 95 suites, with a guest-to-staff ratio of one to one.
Where does Four Seasons I sail?

The Mediterranean in summer, from the Greek islands, Turkey and the Adriatic to the Italian and French Rivieras, and the Caribbean and the Bahamas in winter, mostly from Philipsburg in Sint Maarten, Saint John's in Antigua and Miami. She crosses the Atlantic between the two in spring and autumn.
How much does a voyage on Four Seasons I cost?

Published fares start at US$12,200 per suite for a 3-night Caribbean voyage, and most 7-night sailings start between US$20,000 and US$32,000 per suite. The fare is for the whole suite, not per person.
Are fares on Four Seasons I per person or per suite?
Per suite. Four Seasons Yachts publishes one fare for the suite for the whole voyage, in US dollars, whatever the number of guests the suite sleeps.
What is included in the fare?

The suite, breakfast in designated restaurants, in-suite non-alcoholic drinks and snacks, high-speed Wi-Fi, watersports from the marina, exercise classes subject to availability, meals for children under five, and taxes and port fees.
What is not included?
Lunch and dinner, in-suite dining, alcoholic drinks, spa and salon treatments, shore experiences, laundry, transfers and hotels before and after the voyage.
How many suite types are there on Four Seasons I?
Fourteen, from the Seaview Suite at 44 square metres to the Funnel Suite at 501 square metres on four levels. Every suite has a private terrace.
What is the largest suite on Four Seasons I?
The Funnel Suite: 501 square metres inside on four levels, a 421 square metre terrace, three bedrooms, a private splash pool, an indoor and outdoor gym, a steam room and a personal kitchen.
Can suites connect for families or groups?
Yes. Four Seasons Yachts lists more than 100 connecting combinations, and the Loft Suite joins with up to seven suites for as many as 20 guests.
How long are the voyages?
From 3 to 18 nights. Most are 5 or 7 nights, and consecutive sailings can be joined into a longer voyage.
When did Four Seasons I enter service?
Her first sailing was on 20 March 2026.
Are the pictures photographs?
No. The images here are Four Seasons Yachts' own renderings of the yacht and her suites, and are labelled as renderings.
What are the deposit and cancellation terms?
Ask us. James confirms the deposit, payment dates and cancellation terms for your sailing when he holds a suite.
